study.title: Investigation of Acupuncture-specific BOLD Signal Changes Using Multiband Acquisition and Deconvolution Analysis
study.study_design: Two-group parallel study; within one group two conditions (sham acupuncture and scrubbing) were applied to the same subjects
study.population: 26 healthy right-handed adults (16 men and 10 women) aged 18 to 33 years
study.inclusion_criteria: healthy, right-handed adults aged 18 to 33 years; provided written informed consent

extraction_notes.note: No coordinate table is provided in the paper. All neuroimaging results are presented in Fig. 2 (overlapping group statistical maps) and Fig. 3 (IRF time courses). No MNI or Talairach coordinates are numerically reported in text or tables. All coordinates were extracted as null.

The coordinate space is not explicitly stated in the paper. MNI is inferred from the use of the Montreal Neurological Institute T1-weighted MRI template for normalization, but this was not confirmed in the paper.

Fig. 2 shows overlapping colored statistical activation maps at four axial levels (z=0, 22, 44, 66) across tent functions 1T–13T. No numerical coordinates, cluster sizes, or t-values can be extracted from this figure. Results were extracted as narrative_only.

Fig. 3 shows IRF time-course plots (beta amplitude means ± SE) with significance markers (*P<0.01, **P<0.005, ***P<0.001) but no numerical beta values are reported in the figure or main text. Exact significant time points per region per condition cannot be extracted reliably from the PDF.

Sensory/deqi outcomes were not formally assessed or quantified. The paper mentions 'de-qi' only in the Discussion section as a narrative explanation for the observed BOLD signal pattern. No deqi rating scale was used.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.

The paper states that sham acupuncture and scrubbing were both administered to the same group of 13 subjects (arm_sham_scrub), but it is unclear whether these were counterbalanced across sessions or administered within the same fMRI run. The paper implies they were within the same group but does not clarify the within-subject design for two conditions in arm_sham_scrub.

The paper states that the 3T–10T tent functions 'corresponded to the actual stimulation period.' The stimulation was 15 s at TR=1000ms, meaning 15 TRs. 3T–10T covers 8 TRs (2 TR intervals each = 16 s). The exact correspondence between tent function numbers and time is somewhat ambiguous. Each T interval was stated as 2 s (= 2 TR).

The abstract states 'activated areas were observed in the SII, insula, and thalamus during simulation' for sham acupuncture, while the Results section specifies 'contralateral SI, SII, SMA, the insula, and the thalamus during stimulation (5T–8T)' for sham acupuncture. The abstract omits SI and SMA; the Results text is used as the more complete source.
Randomization procedure is not described. It is stated subjects were 'divided into two groups' but no randomization method is mentioned.
Clinical behavioral outcomes are not reported. This is a neuroimaging study in healthy volunteers with no clinical endpoints.

The exact hemisphere specification for SII activations in sham and scrubbing conditions is not explicitly stated in text (bilateral vs contralateral). For scrubbing, SI is specified as contralateral; SII, insula, thalamus are not specified. Hemisphere was marked as 'not_reported' for these regions.
In the abstract, 'Coclusion' appears instead of 'Conclusion' — this is a typo in the original paper, not an OCR error.

Motion exclusion criteria (e.g., maximum displacement thresholds) are not reported beyond the statement about using soft foam padding. No explicit motion scrubbing or exclusion criteria are described.
